title: The Belfry of Bruges and Other Poems
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
description: The American poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow climbed the belfry in 1842 and wrote two poems about it, imagining the city’s history passing below. They helped make Bruges a stop for American travelers.

title: Bruges-la-Morte
author: Georges Rodenbach
description: A short Symbolist novel by the Belgian writer Georges Rodenbach. A widower moves to Bruges to mourn, and the silent canals and gray streets mirror his grief. It was one of the first novels illustrated with photographs.

title: The Abyss
author: Marguerite Yourcenar
description: Marguerite Yourcenar’s novel about Zeno, a doctor, alchemist, and freethinker in the 1500s, who returns in secret to Bruges and works in a hospital while the Inquisition closes in.

title: Medieval Bruges, c. 850–1550
author: Andrew Brown and Jan Dumolyn
description: Historians Andrew Brown and Jan Dumolyn lead a team of scholars through seven centuries of Bruges: its trade, guilds, revolts, religion, and art. It began on the Burg, the site of the counts’ castle.

title: The Burgundians
author: Bart Van Loo
description: Belgian writer Bart Van Loo’s lively history of the dukes of Burgundy, who ruled the Low Countries in the 1400s and often held court in Bruges. Their palace, the Prinsenhof, is now a hotel.
